clue.text: Very powerful drug has men on it wandering around

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters sit on either side of the drug
letters that go wandering stray from their places, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A drug has sent some men into a confused, aimless state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges MEN ON IT to OMNIENT, and 'around' wraps those letters round POT after the first four.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipotent means all-powerful, a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Eject Judge from historic contest

indicators.note: from says the judge's letter is taken away from the contest

parts.note: a joust was a medieval combat between mounted knights

explanation.surface: A judge is thrown out of an old-time tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to expel or force them out, a synonym.

clue.text: Unfashionable feature of suburban affluence

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wealthy suburbs are mocked for their lack of style.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky or lacking style.

clue.text: Where getting the cup may mean victory?

definitions.text: Where getting the cup may mean victory?

parts.words: Where getting the cup may mean victory?
parts.note: the cup is not a trophy but the hole on a golf course, which a ball goes into at the end of play

explanation.surface: A sporting venue where a trophy is won.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf the hole is also called the cup; sinking the final putt can win the match.
explanation.definitionFit: A putting green is the smooth turf around a golf hole, where the winning stroke often falls.

clue.text: Stories that are old hat, start to finish

indicators.note: the opening letter is taken from the start and sent to the finish

parts.note: something old hat is stale, no longer fresh

explanation.surface: Tired old stories that were dull from beginning to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to finish' moves the first letter S of STALE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales are narratives, a synonym of stories.

clue.text: Err, with amount being incorrect in part of fraction

indicators.note: a wrong arrangement of letters signals they are to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A mistake in a sum leaves part of a fraction wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The numerator is the top number of a fraction, above the line.

clue.text: Be triumphant in college dispute

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone gloats after winning a university argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast or exult over a victory.

clue.text: Curb on newspapers is initially working

parts.note: re means on or concerning
the press is the newspapers collectively

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Restrictions on the newspapers are already in force.
explanation.definitionFit: Repression is restraint or suppression, a synonym of a curb.

clue.text: A quality poet?

parts.note: a poet whose value lies in the value of a single unit of language, the merit of a word

explanation.surface: A tribute to a fine poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as WORD'S WORTH, the poet's name reads as the value of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was the English Romantic poet, here split to mean the value of a single word.

clue.text: to be sure

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'to be sure' (6,4): cut short in the OCR, with no wordplay or definition for SAFETYLAMP, and no scan or search gives the rest.

clue.text: Almost reject egg

indicators.note: almost says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to spurn is to reject scornfully

explanation.surface: A breakfast egg is nearly sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg' is a verb here: to egg someone on.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg on and to spur both mean to urge or encourage.

clue.text: What could be represented as 'Psst!', I wager, eh?

definitions.text: What could be represented as 'Psst!', I wager, eh?

indicators.note: a representation in other letters means the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muttering a bet in hushed tones.
explanation.definitionFit: An aside spoken loudly enough for a theatre audience to hear, like a hissed 'Psst!'.

clue.text: Bland footwear might cover them

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Bland footwear might cover them' (4,8): 'Bland' gives nothing towards PIGSTROTTERS and looks like an OCR misreading; no scan or search shows the printed word.

clue.text: Hunt meet, perhaps, with mass beagle gambolling!

indicators.note: leaping about playfully, so the letters jump into a new order

explanation.surface: Hounds frolic at the gathering before a fox hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: An assemblage is a gathering of people, and a hunt meet is one example.

clue.text: Shocking variety of bugs in dirt

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Many kinds of insects crawling in the soil make an unpleasant sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Disturbing means upsetting or alarming, a synonym.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink's warm it gets people stoned!

parts.note: a sling is a gin-based cocktail, here with its possessive 's
hot means very warm

explanation.surface: A strong cocktail is so potent it gets drinkers high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' means pelted with stones, not intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A catapult fires stones at people, so it literally gets them stoned.

clue.text: Teacher to have importance in calling the register?

parts.note: the head is the head teacher of a school
to count is to matter

explanation.surface: A teacher stresses the importance of taking attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Checking a register is a tally of how many people are present.

clue.text: Love chasing the wind with zest

indicators.note: one piece chasing another comes after it

parts.note: a gust is a sudden blast of wind
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Lovers run through the breeze with enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enthusiasm or relish, a synonym of zest.

clue.text: One knocks back hunt employee, unseating Baron

indicators.note: unseating says a letter is thrown off, removed from the word

parts.note: a beater drives game towards the guns at a shoot

explanation.surface: A hunt worker drinks heavily after a nobleman is thrown from his horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks back' means eats or drinks, not repels.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who consumes food is a diner, one who knocks it back.

clue.text: Starch in a recipe (argument liked with grub)

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe on prescriptions
a row is a quarrel
to root is to dig or grub about

explanation.surface: A cook's instructions call for starch and include a row about food.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowroot is a starch from a tropical plant used to thicken sauces.

clue.text: Method and a firm line in British fiction-that's Barker

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the British fiction

parts.note: a lie is a fiction or falsehood
order means method or system
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A British novel that is orderly and businesslike, written by a famous author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker' looks like a name; it is a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A border collie is a sheepdog breed, and dogs are barkers.

clue.text: Permit hospital to admit one in Scottish town

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to let is to permit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hospital is allowed to take in a patient in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leith is the port district on the Firth of Forth beside Edinburgh.

clue.text: Capital city French friend left wanting to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: A French companion who left wants to go back to a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital of Peru.

clue.text: Banks of Danube, watery and wet

indicators.note: a river's banks are its edges, so take each word's first and last letters

explanation.surface: The Danube's banks are soggy and damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy means moist, covered with droplets.

clue.text: Song one recalled from an opera?

definitions.text: Song one recalled from an opera?

parts.words: Song one recalled from an opera?
parts.note: a solo piece someone hums afterwards, remembered from a night of opera

explanation.surface: A tune remembered after a night at the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo vocal piece in an opera.

clue.text: "A studio losing good man — I help out' — hi-fi enthusiast

indicators.note: losing says the good man's letters are dropped from the studio

parts.note: St, saint, is a good man

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A recording studio loses its best engineer, who offers help to a music lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes ST from STUDIO, leaving UDIO; 'out' rearranges I HELP to PHILE.
explanation.definitionFit: An audiophile is a lover of high-fidelity sound reproduction.

clue.text: Anxious chap, genuinely gutted

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, a chap

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man is truly devastated and nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like 'devastated'; it strips the inside of GENUINELY to leave GY.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means nervous or on edge.

clue.text: Prepared thanks, having got back the cash

indicators.note: got back means the word for thanks is turned backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
the ready is slang for ready money, cash

explanation.surface: Someone is grateful to be repaid their money.
explanation.definitionFit: At the ready means poised and ready for action.
